utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We have a change of interest this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please read aloud the affirmation shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Mr. Behar has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, ma'am, thank you very much for coming here today.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name and your date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I am Aferdita Hajrizi. I was born on the 29th of June, 1964, in Peran village, Podujeve municipality. I am a resident of the town of Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I understand that you in fact grew up and spent most of your life in Mitrovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ma'am, I understand that on June 3rd of 1999 you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor about the events that you experienced in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I understand that you made certain corrections or clarifications to that statement on the 31st of January, 2002; is that also corrected?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read those statements before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the information that's contained in those statements is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender those statements, those first two statements, then they're 65 ter 02319.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00773, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that you also provided a further statement to the Office of the Prosecution on the 20th of August, 2001, and then provided a brief correction to that statement on the 6th of March, 2002; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to read those statements before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the information contained in those statements are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I would then seek to tender those statements as well that's 65 ter 02320.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And they will received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be assigned P00774, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ms. Hajrizi, do you recall testifying at the trial of Slobodan Milosevic on the 26th of April, 2002.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And have you had the chance to review the transcript of your testimony in that trial?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that there were two things in that transcript that you'd like to clarify or explain for us so that it accurately reflects your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could I have up on the screen 65 ter number 02321. I'll need page T3899.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have these on my screen also, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, they're just coming up, ma'am. I think you should be able to see it.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: It will be in English. I know you speak a little bit of English.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: It's good. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I can read it out as well for you so that we have a translation. I see that at lines 5, 6, and 7 there's a sentence that may be somewhat unclear. I'll read it out. It says: "Pllana is not my -- is the son of my aunt, Skender Pllana, who on the next day -- he was -- donned a uniform, and on the next day he put on another uniform ..." Are you able to explain or clarify that sentence for us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be very brief. I believe that this technique of correcting the transcript is not right. If something needs to be clarified, it can be done by questions during the testimony of the witness. I believe that this way of changes that are going to be made to the transcript several years later and -- is simply not correct. Thank you. It could have been done during the re-direct at that trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is the position, Mr. Djurdjic, that a witness who gave evidence some seven years ago has been asked very recently whether -- to read the transcript of that evidence and whether that is correct. The witness, from what little we've heard so far, says that in two or so respects there's something that is not clear or needs correction. The witness is being asked to indicate what it is that the witness wants to change. There seems to be nothing either unfair or improper in that process. The witness will tell us what it is that she feels is not correct. So please carry on, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ms. Hajrizi, I don't know if you -- would you prefer me to read the sentence back to you again or are you able to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is before me. I already read it. These are some technical mistakes. This is Agim's son -- son of Agim's aunt, Skender Pllana. There is something mixed up about the uniform. The uniform refers to Nenad, not to a civilian, not to a relative, so in my opinion this is just a technical mistake nothing else. This is what I wanted to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So just to clarify then, it appears to me from what you're saying that there's really two sentences there or two ideas, the first being that Pllana is the son of your aunt, Skender Pllana, and then the other idea being that the next day he - and you're saying Nenad - had put on another uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, here I'm talking about the day after the crime was committed. On that day in the vicinity of my house, Nenad patrolled wearing a police uniform. He had committed a crime in my house during the night, whereas Skender Pllana is a family member, he's a relative. The person wearing a police uniform was the policeman, Nenad Pavicevic, whereas Skender Pllana is a family member who came close to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. I think that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can I have up page 3901.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think this will be more straightforward. Ms. Hajrizi, I see at line 2 -- well, 1 and 2 there's a reference saying: " ... at which my father-in-law and Agim were present ..." This is during the killings that you're referring to. Is there something you wanted to clarify about that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Again, a small technical mistake, I guess an interpretation mistake. My father-in-law died 24 years ago. This should read my mother-in-law, who was also killed on that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. With those changes now made, does this transcript accurately reflect your evidence and would you testify to the same facts again today?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender this transcript that's 65 ter number 02321.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned as P00775, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, Ms. Hajrizi, do you recall testifying at the trial of Milan Milutinovic et al. at the 26th of September, 2006?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review the transcript of your testimony in that trial?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that there was one line as well that you wished to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 05052 at page 4047. It's down at about line 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You had indicated that you wanted to clarify a line you found confusing, that's at line 18, it's a quote; it says -- I'll just read it out to you. It says: "'If anything happens to me, because you know that they are not this by accident, wearing uniforms and heavily armed, they're here to commit a crime.'" Are you able to clarify that for us, what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. These were my husband's words. A few moments before the crime was committed he said, If anything happens to me, don't forget these names because these policemen in front of our door are not there by accident. We all know they're here to commit a crime. So the quote should read, Don't forget these names in case anything happens to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. I think that's much clearer now. Now that we've made that change, does this transcript accurately reflect your evidence and would you testify to the same facts again today?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would seek to tender 65 ter number 05052.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned as P00776, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I would also seek to tender one exhibit that was tendered in association with Ms. Hajrizi's testimony in the Milutinovic trial and the Milosevic trial, it was part of her 92 bis package at that time. That's Exhibit 00051. I can indicate that that's the judgement of the Mitrovica district court in the case of the murder of Agim Hajrizi. It was discussed in her testimony in Milutinovic as well. I can give the transcript cite, it was page 4050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned as P00777, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I can now provide a brief summary for Ms. Hajrizi's evidence. Ms. Hajrizi lived in Kosovska Mitrovica with her family. She describes the persecution faced by Kosovo Albanians and the threats and harassment experienced by her family in particular prior to the armed conflict in 1999. Ms. Hajrizi's husband was Agim Hajrizi, a well-known advocate for the rights of Albanian workers. In the early morning hours of the 25th of March, 1999, two cars drove to the house where Ms. Hajrizi's family lived. Six policemen wearing blue camouflage uniforms and black berets forced their way into the house. They murdered Agim Hajrizi along with Ms. Hajrizi's oldest son Ilir and Mr. Hajrizi's mother. Ms. Hajrizi and her surviving children managed to hide and after the murders they moved to a house in the Tavnik neighbourhood of Mitrovica. On the 28th of March, 1999, Serb forces began burning houses and telling people to leave. Ms. Hajrizi and her children joined a large column of people fleeing to Zabare village. After three days they were told by the police there to go back to the Mitrovica. The situation that she describes in Mitrovica was terrible with shooting and burning throughout the town. They spent several days there before boarding buses that Serb forces had arranged to transport Kosovo Albanians across the border to Montenegro. That is the conclusion of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ma'am, I have some brief questions for you in the limited time we have remaining. We heard some evidence earlier in this trial about your husband Agim Hajrizi. And I know you explained in your previous testimony that Mr. Hajrizi worked to defend the rights of Albanian workers in Mitrovica, that he was a prominent figure in the Albanian community. Can you explain to this Court when Mr. Hajrizi began to be threatened?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: My husband, Agim Hajrizi, had graduated from the Faculty of Economics and was working in the battery factory in Mitrovica. In 1989, when the constitution was revoked, all Albanian workers were dismissed from work, my husband being one of them. Mitrovica is an industrial town, Your Honours. When the autonomy of Kosovo was revoked and when people were dismissed from work, Trepca was the only company where people could work at the time. The dire social situation forced the people to form trade unions that would assist the innocent Albanian population. At that time, my husband took upon himself to perform this duty. He -- his main intention was to help the working class and not to harm anyone. He began to be persecuted from that time; and until the night when he was killed, arrests, beatings, persecutions were ongoing, they never stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am. You described in your statement the manner in which your husband was killed, by a group of six men that included Nenad Pavicevic. You also described that you knew Mr. Pavicevic to be a policeman. Can you explain how it was that you knew that Mr. Pavicevic was a police officer?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: That Nenad Pavicevic was a policeman, member of the Serb police forces at the time, this I know from the moment he got an employment with the Serb police forces. He was our first-door neighbour, as I have already mentioned in my statements. Every day we had the opportunity to see him in a police uniform. That Nenad was the person who participated in the killing of my husband, my son, and my mother-in-law. This can be proved by the fact that I saw him with my own eyes in the yard, in my courtyard. He was armed and in a group of five other people, five other policemen, who were trying to enter our house, to break into our house, and this is what they did. This is what I saw with my own eyes. I saw Nenad Pavicevic's face with my own eyes during the night of the crime. I saw him in our courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ma'am, are you able to tell us what uniform those men were wearing, those six men that you just described, at that time?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Until the night of the crime, Nenad Pavicevic and three others whom we recognised were wearing regular police uniforms. By "regular" I mean blue trousers and blue shirt. On the night of the crime, however, Nenad Pavicevic and his group, the remaining five policemen, were wearing a different uniform. This was a camouflage uniform, blue, and dark or black pattern. They were wearing black berets on their heads and carrying weapons on their shoulders. So this uniform was a camouflage uniform, blue/black pattern, and they had berets on their heads and were carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, I'll have a couple of questions for you about the things that happened after you left your house that night, after these killings had taken place. When you described what was happening at that time in Mitrovica, and I believe this would be on the 25th of March, you used the -- you make the statement that: "I could not decide what to do about my situation because of a lot of presence of the police ..." Can you tell us what you meant by that, and in particular what you observed the police doing at that time?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. You're probably referring to the time after the crime was committed in my house; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was 12.45 a.m. I was left alone with my two children. I had to find a way out, a way to leave the house. I went to my neighbours, to a house, which is about 100 metres far from our house. The centre of the town was filled with policemen and soldiers wearing different kinds of uniforms. I had to leave the centre because the life of my children and my own life was at risk. This is what I've already explained in my statement, and I can elaborate on it today if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ma'am, at page 4 of your second statement you described joining a big column of fleeing people and seeing dead bodies, and you described as well that there were Serb forces at the front of this convoy directing it. Can you explain to the Court how it was that they were directing the convoy, how it was that they were getting people to move?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The armed groups, police and military, were attacking the population in their own homes; and it's understandable that there is nothing like home. You could hear shots being fired. I don't know what they were. At that moment, the home was on fire and members of the families were being pushed out onto the street under the firing of shots, terrified, beaten, maltreated; and I have told that I have seen bodies, people who were killed on the streets, and all of them were violently dragged out of their houses and they were shouted at and told and screamed at, Go there, this is not your place; go to Albania, that is your place. So they were massively deporting people from their own homes, from their ethnic territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. I know that you also described in the convoy at that time that there was some shooting. I believe you said that it was something to the effect of it was going over people's heads. Can you explain that to us, how that was taking place and your understanding of why.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: All the way along which we were travelling all our moves were forced upon us by these police and military forces, armed police and military forces. We were under the threat of weapons and rounds of ammunitions being fired. They were trying to terrify the population by firing weapons in the air so that they could leave their homes and flee. I have heard a lot of bursts of fire, a lot of screams on the part of policemen and soldiers, Serb policemen and soldiers, and that was terrifying I tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ma'am, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I can just indicate to the Chamber the reference for what I was previously referring to, it's in the statement that was 2320. I'm not sure what exhibit that's been made but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this the second --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit P773, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. And that was at page 4 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ma'am, thank you, thank you very much for your evidence today. Those are my questions, and now my learned colleague for the Defence will have some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Should I correct myself? 774, Mr. Behar. Mr. Djurdjic, you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Hajrizi. My name is Veljko Djurdjic, a member of the Defence team of the accused, General Djordjevic; along with me is Ms. Marie O'Leary, a member of our Defence team. First of all I would like to extend my condolences to you for the loss of your loved ones, both on my behalf and on behalf of my client. I have a few questions relating to parts of your statements that you've given subsequent to your first one. My first question would be: At what time was your memory the most fresh? The first statement was given in 1999, then 2002, and then we have testimonies that you gave in the Milutinovic and Milosevic cases, and yet again we see today that there are some corrections required to be made in those statements.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: What was the question? When was my memory fresher?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As times goes by, does your memory of a certain event become more clear and fresher?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Your Honours, despite all the suffering and what I went through and all that I've been through to this day, I would like to thank God that I have managed to keep my memory. I am very clear in my mind about what happened, from the moment that it happened to this day. So all the corrections that have been made, you may understand that there may be mistakes during translation, but I would never change anything from what I've been through and experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hajrizi. Let me start from something that I immediately spotted. You said that after the event on the night of the 25th which took place at 12.45, during night, you left your house and you saw a crowd of policemen and army personnel. In your 1999 statement, that is, page 10 in the Albanian version, paragraph 4; English page 8, paragraph 3, you said that you first went to your neighbour's and that only later somebody told you that there were soldiers and policemen in the centre of the town. That's Exhibit P773.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I've already explained that the moment the crime was committed I went to my neighbour's, but when I had to leave the place where I took shelter that night, then we are talking about a six-hour difference, I have seen large numbers of police and army forces on the way to going to meeting my brother. I think I'm clear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see them that night when you were leaving, the police and the army, as you said today, it rather happened during the following day, that was the 26th of March when you were on your way to meet your brother. Is that what you're saying today?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No, no. It was the 25th of March. It was the same day. It wasn't the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at your 1999 statement, page 10, paragraph 4, this is what I have drawn your attention to, and I even recounted certain parts. In fact, you never mentioned any army troops. You just say that somebody else told you about the army the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For Your Honours in the English that's page 8, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that what I've just told you is not contained in your 1999 statement?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Is this the page which is on the screen in front of me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The one beginning: "Kur u largova ..."

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: "When I left my house with the children, I went to the homes of some friends of mine who lived nearby. In that house there was no one, so I knocked on the door of an elderly man and his wife ..." This was in the moments after the crime when I took shelter in the house of my neighbour, and I told you about the moment when I left my home I took shelter in my neighbour's home; and when I had to leave my neighbour's home to go and join and meet my brother, that was the morning of the 25th of March and our town was filled up with Serb police and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hajrizi, yes, this is what you said today but as for your direct knowledge it is not there in this first paragraph, but let us leave this to the Bench to assess. Another thing that I noticed during your testimony today --

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I'd like to say something more, if I may. You better try and read carefully and better and see what I want to say. I've said in my statements all that I have been through and seen and all that I know. If you want to read it, it's there; if you don't, it's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, I'm doing my best, and I'm really trying to point you to those parts of your statement that I believe are contrary to your -- today's testimony. That is why I, in all fairness, showed you this paragraph that I referred to, and in the light of your responses I will leave it up to Their Honours to evaluate your answers. If you believe that I wasn't doing my job fairly and properly, please say so, but if you have this direct knowledge contained in this paragraph and that all this happened that same night, then I'm ready to apologise for a mistake. You also said today that on the night of the 25th you looked out the window and saw an armed group of six armed policemen. Let me again refer you to your first statement given in 1999, that's page 6 in English, paragraph 2, and page 7, paragraph 3 in the Albanian, where you say - and I'm going to read it - "I couldn't see what kind of weapons they had if they had any, but I knew that they didn't have rifles. I couldn't discern whether they wore any patterns or emblems on their uniforms."

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I've said other times, and I will say it now, after ten years I do not know what type of weapons there are and I do not want to know them. I didn't know what type of weapons they were carrying, and I do not want to know because the weapon is the worst thing that exists. That's why I don't want to know. Your Honours, I would like to tell you that there were six armed policemen in front of our house. I do not know what type of weapons they were carrying, and I don't want to know what type of weapons they were carrying to this day. I know they were long weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said today that in 1989 Kosovo's autonomy was revoked. Can you explain to us what you meant by that? Can you explain that in more detail, please.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: You know better what it means and what meaning it had, revoking the autonomy. I do not want to go any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said today that in 1989 all the Albanians were sacked from their jobs. Where did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: This was a piece of information that even the youngest child knew about. My Arianit, son who was very young, he knew about; and he knew that his father went to work every day but then when he was dismissed he understood that he was jobless. It's understandable how everybody knew about it. The question is irrelevant I think. It doesn't make any sense to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you moved to Kosovska Mitrovica when you were a young girl. In some documents it says, in fact, that you were born in Kosovska Mitrovica. Can you tell me specifically which documents say that your place of birth is Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. In my valid documents, up until the moment that we moved from one town to another they say that my birthplace is the village of Peran in the Podujeve municipality. And after you move to a place, then you can have the place of birth as the place where you initially lived. I moved to Mitrovica when I was only four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your current documents, does Kosovska Mitrovica feature as your birthplace?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who issued these documents to you?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: If you're interested to get further information on that, you may ask the authorities there. These are valid documents which are issued by the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Hajrizi, on the 3rd of June, 1999, you gave a statement to the OTP investigators of this Tribunal. How did it come about for you to give this statement at all?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: After the crime that was committed in my house, my only wish was to cooperate with an institution who would find out and bring the truth out into the open. I came and contacted The Hague Tribunal. It's an institution which I have great respect about, and I'd like to thank them wholeheartedly for what they've done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us, please, how did you establish a contact, and where did you give this statement?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: All that you would like to know about my statements and these things, you can refer to the statements and the documents in front of you and you will find everything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, my question was: Where did you give your statement to an OTP investigator, in which country?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: My answer was: Get hold of my first statement, and if you read it you will find the facts, the real -- the correct facts there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If there had been such information, Mrs. Hajrizi, I would not have asked you about the place where you gave your statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I said my statement, my first statement, if you have it in front of you, it will say exactly where I have made my statement. It is in front of me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I can't see that. That's why I'm asking you this question. I can't find it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying it. You read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let me say, Mrs. Hajrizi, that I have what I believe is a copy of the statement, and it doesn't tell me where the statement was made. But you may have something on yours which tells you, but it's not on what I have, and I think Mr. Djurdjic may have the same as I have. Could you help me, please, by letting me know where it was that you made the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I made this statement on the 3rd of June, 1999, in the house of my brother, Fitim Ismaili, who lives in Groningen, in the Netherlands, since 20 years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That helps me a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Hajrizi, can you tell me, please, when did your husband become president of the Assembly of Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Are you saying as the chairman of the local government in Mitrovica? It's on the second page of my -- of my first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please explain how come he was elected. Who elected him?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: He was elected by his co-residents. He was elected by the people for whom he was working and who he was trying to help, that is, the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So these were the elections in which only members of the Albanian community voted?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The Serbs were those who exercised violence upon us, and it was normal that the Albanians had to find a leader of their own who would help and lead them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If this translation is correct, you said that he was the chairman of the local government in shadow. Can you explain what this "in shadow" means.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, I said it clearly that 1989 was the year when Kosovo's autonomy was revoked, and the need arose for something Albanian to start to operate, something parallel, parallel institutions to the benefit of the Albanians to protect them and to organise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, I did not insist on this answer but now you repeat it once again, that the autonomy of Kosovo was revoked in 1989. Could you explain how it was revoked, because you keep repeating this conclusion. So could you maybe tell us how this came about?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: It's a question that you can normally ask but it's a question the answer to which you very well know. When all schools are closed, factories are closed down, people are dismissed from their jobs, and nothing works for a people, what do you call this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, did you work at that time, in 1989?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes. I was a good mother to my children, a good wife to my husband, and I had a very important job at the time: Looking after the children and their education.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At Kosovska Mitrovica in the second half of 1990s, was there a local television station and what kind?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: There was a television station in Mitrovica and the only TV station in Mitrovica was the one in Serbo-Croat language. It was a television station of Serbia; nothing in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your husband have any press conferences at that TV station?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No, because my husband did not recognise the Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether there was any formal procedure instigated against your husband due to his activities?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Could you please explain what you mean by "procedure." You mean court proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean either criminal proceedings or misdemeanour proceedings due to his political activities.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Criminal? I apologise, but my husband was not engaged in criminal activities. To defend the rights of your own people, to defend an innocent population living in a dire social situation, this is not a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, I asked this because you mentioned during your testimony on several occasions your husband was arrested, taken to the Secretariat of the Interior. This is why I'm asking whether there was any criminal persecution, whether he was the subject of any criminal proceedings to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: From 1989 up until 1999, that is the night when he was killed by the Serb police, my husband was taken to the police many, many times, where he was beaten, ill treated, detained. He was arrested in the presence of my youngest son, Arianit. I've explained this very well in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was whether there were any criminal proceedings against him and whether you are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Arrests, beatings, ill treatment, and the final act, the killing itself, is not enough? There was a necessity for criminal proceedings to be instituted against him - this is what you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking whether there were any criminal proceedings and whether you know that there were or were not any criminal proceedings. This is all that I asked.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: That's what I already answered, that for many years violence was exercised upon him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. You said in your statement from 1999, you're talking about the events in 1998, and you said that you were aware of the conflict in Kosovo. Could you explain what was this conflict. This is the part of your statement on page 3, the very last paragraph on page 3, and in the English version it is paragraph 1 on page 3.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The violence, killings, maltreatments, persecutions committed by the authorities of the Milosevic regime against the Albanian people made the conflict itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And there was no reaction from the other side; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Everything coming from the side, the side of the Albanian, was peaceful resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what Kosovo Liberation Army is?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to talk about these matters. This is not why I'm here. I'm here to explain to what happened to my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But in your statement you did mention the KLA. This is why I'm asking this.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I did not mention the KLA. I mentioned several persons who called themselves KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is exactly why I'm asking what "KLA" means. Do you know what it means?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me under which circumstances you met these people who you said told you that they were KLA members?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: These persons came to my house as normal civilians in August 1998 - and this is to prove that my memory serves me right - at the time when Lazar Gligorovski was trying to attack our house. These were people who knew how good, willing, my husband was towards his own people. He came to our house and offered assistance to my husband, but as I already mentioned, my husband was against violence. He resisted peacefully all his life, and he chose peaceful resistance even on this occasion. He replied to them by using this words and I quote, I want to live in Mitrovica, to continue to live here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What kind of service did these members of the KLA offer to your husband?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: There are different kinds of assistance. If you want to leave your house, we can find you another place to stay, if you want to avoid any conflicts with Lazar, this type of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. They didn't offer to kill Lazar?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: In the heat of a moment people will say, I could kill him or her, whatever, but my husband was always against killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we have mentioned your neighbour, Lazar, is it true that the police filed misdemeanour charges against him?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The Serb police first tasked Lazar with a specific task: To kill Hajriz, to attack Hajriz's house and his family members, and the mere fact of misdemeanour charges filed against him is just a farce, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that misdemeanour proceedings were instigated against him, that it was determined that he was under the influences of alcohol when he fired in the air and also disturbed you and your family? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Whenever someone wants to conceal a crime, he will say that he was under alcohol or drugs or whatever. He didn't look to me like someone who was drunk or drugged. He looked quite normal to me when he did what he did to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that he was sanctioned at a misdemeanour court for what he did?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that because I took part in this trial, and after an hour and a half of testimony as an eye-witness to what Lazar had committed against our family -- however, he was declared not guilty under pretext of lack of facts, although I was there, an eye-witness, a person who had seen everything that he had done. Does this procedure look normal, regular procedure to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, we are talking about two different events. I haven't come to the point yet that you are just describing. I'm asking you now about the events from August 1998, when this gentleman, your neighbour, fired into the air, fired a rifle into the air. And for that particular incident he was found guilty.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: And this is what I'm talking about. To attempt on someone's life, to try to kill someone, and to be sentenced to only three months imprisonment, this is absurd; and it is not true that he fired into the air. The bullet hit our house, and there is to this day a bullet mark on the walls of our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So for the event that occurred in August 1998 he was imprisoned for three months. Could you tell me now whether you know Mr. Halimi Mehmet? Maybe I can explain. This gentleman comes from Kosovska Mitrovica and he was an attorney-at-law; I believe he still is to this day.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: If you're referring to a certain person, you should use his or her correct name. I don't know Mehmet Halimi. What I know, who I know, is Mahmut Halimi, a lawyer from Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Hajrizi, you are right, it is Mr. Mahmut Halimi. I'm sorry. I had it written down wrongly. So do you know Mr. Mahmut Halimi?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I came to know him after my husband was killed, in 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did your husband maybe tell you before the year 2000, so in mid-1990s when he was engaged in trade union activities, did he ever talk to you about Mr. Mahmut Halimi, attorney-at-law, and their cooperation?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: My husband had so many friends, acquaintances, and associates, so I can't really recall this particular person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These persons who came to your house after your neighbour fired his weapon and they said that they were members of the KLA, am I right to say that they wore civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, normal clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that you didn't see that they had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Well, I cannot put a person wearing normal clothes and a weapon at the same time together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that these persons who said they were members of the KLA were colleagues from the trade unions of your husband and they used to be members of trade unions?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. You see how much time has elapsed because in 1999 when you gave your statement you knew that they were members of the trade union. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: That is what I heard at the time. I heard that they had been trade union members, but I didn't know myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know the names of these persons who came to your house, to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No. I never knew their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember when the verification mission came to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes, in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that upon their arrival the situation did not improve. What was the situation like at the time when they came?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The Serb repression continued. The Serb authorities did not stop their violence against the Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe the time has come for a technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you near the end of your questions, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must now have the first break, in which the tapes are rewound. We will resume again at 11.00. In the break, the court officer will assist you, as you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, I promised the Chamber that I will finish my cross-examination shortly, therefore kindly listen carefully to my questions and if possible give me precise answers. Do you agree with me that Nenad Pavicevic was a neighbour of yours?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: A police neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From very early childhood, Nenad Pavicevic was a nuisance to you and your family, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: That was part of his upbringing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was exactly going to say that he had poor upbringing. Am I right in saying that you were afraid of him?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Because he didn't behave in a normal way, to put it like that.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I've given all the details of what he did. He behaved like an uneducated kid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that that night you saw the cars in which these persons arrived in front of your house. Do you remember the make of those cars?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No. There was no time for me to study what type of vehicles they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Am I right in saying that this crime was reported by Mr. Skender Pllana on the 26th in the morning to Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, Secretariat of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No, you're not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me then who did report the crime?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Those who committed the crime, Your Honours, reported the crime. The very fact that among them there was six policemen, members of the Serbian police force, who committed the crime, they returned to the crime scene for a second time and steal all the articles they needed and what was needed to the Milosevic regime. And for the third time, when they come to patrol in front of our house and they look for a member of my family, it's understandable who has done that. It's those who committed the crime - it's the Serb policemen who killed three members of my family - they were the ones who reported the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the morning of the 26th, did the investigating judge of the county court of Kosovska Mitrovica visited the scene and was the deputy public prosecutor also present during an on-site investigation; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Your Honours, each time they mention the date of the 26th of March, it's not the 26th of March, it's the 25th of March. And as for who came to uncover the crime or who reported the crime, I wasn't there. I wasn't there who came to investigate the crime because I wasn't there. I've only heard about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You could have told me that straight away, Mrs. Hajrizi. Let us now go back to the correction that you made today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the transcript from Milosevic case, 65 ter P775, page 3899, lines --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Or rather, let's start from the top with the question and then we'll get to your answer. I will try and translate it. The question was: "Do you know that your uncle or maybe your husband's uncle reported the incident to the president of the court? M. Ivanovic ... was any report filed about this crime?" And your answer was: "You have wrongful information. He's not my uncle. He's the son of my aunt." And then you went on to say that first he was in one uniform and later on you said that he was wearing a different uniform.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: A little while earlier I explained it wasn't Skender Pllana who is the son of the aunt of Agim who informed the court -- or the judge about what happened. Skender Pllana was called as the next of kin in the absence of my children to identify the bodies, to identify the bodies. This is enough I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajrizi, I cannot show you the document that you are not familiar with at this point, but I would like now to finish with making comparisons between your statements given in 1999 and 2001 and your testimonies. And please, if we can be speedy and efficacious. Madam, this is P774, the statement of the 20th of August, 2001, and I'm going to make some comparisons with your 1999 statement. On page 4 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the counsel to repeat the pages slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- there is no mention of that in your 1999 version of the statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me just repeat the pages. Albanian version page 4, paragraph 6; English version page 4, paragraph 3. In 2001 you said: "On the morning of the 28th of March, 1999, the Serbs started burning houses and expelling people from Tavnik," whereas this has not been mentioned at all in your statement given in June 1999. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's move on. In the next paragraph, second sentence, you say: "They started burning houses at one end of the streets where we were and people were told to leave immediately." And then you said: "The soldiers were shooting and shouting. They were very aggressive. A house of Halit Barani which was 50 metres from ours was burnt." In your 1999 statement there is again no mention of this. Do you agree with me, Mrs. Hajrizi?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: What has been added in the second statement is an addition. This is additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the following paragraph, sentence number 3, it says: "In the street where we lived I saw dead bodies of people who had been killed." This also doesn't feature in your 1999 statement, Mrs. Hajrizi.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Not in the road where we lived but in the road where my family lived. This is an additional bit of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We now move on to page 5, paragraph 2, in Albanian and the same page in English, the next paragraph. You say: "When we arrived in Zabare during -- in the afternoon we heard reports of the radio station Deutsche Welle that there were 700.000 [as interpreted] displaced persons in Zabare." This quotation also is not contained in your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: 70.000. Please, it's 70.000, not 700.000. What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that it's not in your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: This is an additional bit of information too. This is an addition. It's the truth. It's quite true actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The first sentence in the next passage reads: "In front of the column were the Serbian units who were directing us towards the village." There is nothing like this in your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The same applies to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to facilitate for the Chamber the following of these exchanges, I'm talking about the last paragraph on page 8 in English and the last two paragraphs on page 9. Mrs. Hajrizi, in the next paragraph, that's paragraph 4, page 5, in Albanian and in English you said in 2001 that: "Each newcomer told us about dead people and we lived under tremendous psychological pressure." There is no such statement in your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I say this again. If I missed something then I can say it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the next paragraph you've been talking throughout it about the 29th of March and the burial of four people and you mention also the family, et cetera. I was unable to find that portion in your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I have expounded on this a second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But it's not in your first statement. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: It's in other statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. English version page 5, paragraph 3; Albanian version page 5, paragraph 6, you say: "I saw paramilitary units in Zabare. They were dressed in camouflage dark blue uniforms mixed with black batches, high heels, gloves, and they had big knives." This does not appear in your 1999 statement; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: This is a more detailed and the best description of what happened. This is in the second statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: High boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: There is no such description in your first statement.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: This has been a more detailed explanation, description, in this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Hajrizi. On page 5, paragraph 8 in English; and page 6, paragraph 13 in Albanian, you said: "There was still shooting and burning in the town. We didn't dare venture out, and we stayed indoors all the time." In your 1999 statement there is no mention of the burning.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: I'm surprised that you don't know that they were massively burning houses at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Hajrizi, but I wasn't there so therefore I couldn't know. I know that you gave a statement in 1999 in which you also didn't mention that. I'm also interested about your travel to Montenegro. First of all, you didn't say that it was the Serbs who provided buses, but before that let me ask you was your brother a taxi-driver?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What kind of car did he have?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Can I make a clarification. You -- maybe you're expecting that. It was impossible for my brother to take his car with him because the Serbian police and army would not allow him to take his property with him. That's why they had put buses, the Serb authorities put buses at the disposal of the people, so that they could take the people away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your second statement you said that you travelled by bus and you said that you had to pay the fare. Did you pay any bus fare? because that's what it says in your 2001 statement?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: We were forced out of our homes, and we were forced to pay for our seats on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the English version on page 6, paragraph 4; or in the Albanian version page 7, paragraph 4, you stated when you came to Mehov Breg men were forced out of the buses, they were abused and questioned about their contacts with the KLA. There is no such statement in the statement -- in the testimony that you gave in 1999.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Again, this is additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, Mrs. Hajrizi, where did you cross the border between Albania and the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: From Ulqin or maybe you should read it in the statement, it's explained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ulcinj, in which republic is that town situated?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: You know very well where Ulqin is situated, it's in Montenegro, a republic that broke away from former Yugoslavia, and now it's an independent state.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Hajrizi. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. With this I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Behar, is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. Just a few brief questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Ms. Hajrizi, you were asked a number of questions about your neighbour Lazar Gligorovski, and in your testimony in the Milutinovic case you described what happened after Mr. Gligorovski fired these shots at your house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If I could have up P776 at page 4057. This is at about line 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, you said in that case - and this is beginning at line 6: "You mean my neighbour Merciba, who later told me that the Serb police when they were taking Lazar Gligorovski down the steps and beating him, they asked him: 'Why did you not carry out your duty when you took this rifle?' And you understand very well, I think, what that means." Can you explain to us what that does mean, so in other words when they said "Why did you not carry out your duty," what did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: The Serb authorities, Milosevic regime, had distributed weapons to people who were expected to carry out designated tasks and duties. One of them was Lazar Gligorovski. He had been issued with a weapon by the Serb police in order to commit a crime against us. Once he did not hit any of members of my family, two or three hours later the police came and said to him, Once you were issued this weapon, why did you fail to carry out your task? This means that his task was to kill us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You were also asked some questions about whether an investigative judge attended the scene after these killings took place. Now -- perhaps before I ask the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could just have up P775, that's at page 3899.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So when this investigative judge was at the scene, was Nenad Pavicevic also at the scene at the same time?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I understand from your previous testimony that this investigative judge asked about whether the closest relatives would come to identify the bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you indicated that you were told that Nenad Pavicevic made some comments at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think if we can just scroll down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You described Nenad Pavicevic saying: "' ... where is Aferdita and the two children? I want her to come here ...'" Can you explain your understanding of what he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: Considering the fact that three members of our six-member family were killed and three survived, I understand his words very well. He was looking for the remaining three members of my family. Your Honours, this showed clearly to me that the orders from the Milosevic authorities were for my entire family to be eliminated. So Nenad Pavicevic, with his group of policemen, was tasked to eliminate the entire Hajrizi family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And finally - and this is again just another point of clarification - you were asked some questions about crossing a border or the border. It was my understanding from your statements that you, in fact, crossed two borders. Can you explain which was the first border you crossed.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: First we crossed the Kosovo-Montenegro border, and second the Montenegro-Albanian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: AFERDITA HAJRIZI
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- pleased to know that that concludes your questioning. We have all of our statements and the amplifications of them and the transcript of your evidence in the two previous trials, and we've heard of course all that you've been able to say today. We're very grateful for that and that you've been able to come here yet again to assist us. We thank you, and you may now return to your normal activities. The court officer will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to extend my gratitude to you, to this Tribunal, for giving us the opportunity, ordinary people who've been through a lot during the war, to tell the truth and to bring justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Nilsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The next witness will be Mr. Rahim Latifi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Would you please read aloud the affirmation shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. I think Ms. Nilsen has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry. Mr. Latifi, could you please state your full name and birth date for the record.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Rahim Latifi. I was born on the 14th of May, 1970.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: In the village of Peran, Prizren municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And do you still live in this village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, I still live there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecution on the 28th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to read through this statement before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: On the 16th and 17th of October, 2006, you testified in the Milutinovic et al. case. Did you have the chance to review the transcript with a language assistant before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the information contained in your statement from 1999 together with your transcript from your previous testimony is true and accurate to the best of your belief and knowledge, and would you provide the same answers today?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Then I seek to tender this statement and the transcript into evidence. It's 65 ter number 02381 the statement and 05031 for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First the statement will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00778, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00779, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I would now read out the court summary for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: The witness describes events from 24th of March, 1999, when Serb police and military with tanks and other vehicles surrounded the village of Pirane in Prizren municipality. The village was shelled and houses were burnt by police who were armed with weapons which the witness describes as guns that set houses on fire. On the 24th of March, 1999, some residents of Pirane left for the village of Mamusha right nearby, whilst the witness and others went in a convoy towards the village of Srbica. On the way to Srbica, village snipers killed one convoy member and injured at least one other. Soon after arriving in the village, the police started to shoot at the tractors in the convoy the witness were present. The witness remained in Srbica for about a month until the chief of police from Prizren ordered village leaders to inform anyone not originally from Srbica that they had to go to Albania. The witness describes a big Serb offensive on the 25th of April, 1999, in the area of Srbica when Serbs shelled villages of Donji Retimlje and Randobrava. On the following day, the witness hired a bus and travelled to the village of Zur, west of Prizren municipality. Towards the border at Morina they went, and at the border ID documents were taken from them. The witness describes seeing the police burying bodies, and on the 27th and the 28th of March in the area of Pirane he saw two police trucks on the road from Krusha e Madhe with bodies inside. The witness is a key eye-witness to deportation and burning. His house was close to the main road and he therefore had a good view of vehicles arriving the village on the 24th and the 25th of March, 1999. He describes perpetrators, their vehicles, and weapons, and he is an eye-witness to the police burying bodies and transporting them from Pirane. The witness is an eye-witness to the shelling of Pirane mosque. This is the end of the court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the witness's thorough statement and transcript now is tendered and received, I do not have any further questions for the witness at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honours. Thank you. Once again I can't find my way through this summary read out by the OTP. It seems that the summary that I have is a different one, so some sentences that were read out do not exist in mine and neither in the Serbian or in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Latifi, could you please tell me the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Xhemali.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Xhemajl or Xhemali?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Xhemali.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I heard that, thank you. Could you tell me what is your mother tongue?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the population of Pirane in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: About 2.700 or 2.800 I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know the villagers of Pirane well?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In March of 1999, who did you live with?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: My wife, my children, my parents, and my brother with his children.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All of you lived in a same household?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me whether your family house had a courtyard.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, we do have a courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this courtyard encircled by a wall?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what was this wall made of?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Concrete bricks, five layers of bricks. I would say about 1.20 to 1.50 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there an entrance gate to the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what was this gate made of, so what material and how high was it?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The gate was made of wood, about 1-centimetre thick wood, and it was about 2 and a half metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you closing that gate at night?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did your father do? I'm sorry, I have to ask this because I concluded from your statement that he was alive in the -- in March of 1999, so what did he do?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: He's still alive. We were in farming. We were farmers, but none of us was employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, the brother who lived with you in the same household, how old was he?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: At that time, my brother lived in Germany. My two elder brothers lived in Germany at the time. This one was born in 1966.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, where was your house situated in Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Close to the main Prizren-Gjakove road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that your house was in the plain?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, it is in a plain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, please tell me whether you were a member of any political party in 1999 or in the earlier period.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your studies, were you an active member of any student movements?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, you mentioned that there was a parallel municipal government in your village. Could you please explain to us what that means.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: There was the LDK, the Kosova Democratic League, who dealt with the problems of the villagers, especially those dealing with education.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I first asked you whether you were a member of any political party, and you said no; however, my next question related to the parallel authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we see exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D003-0112, please. Page 3642, lines 17 and 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sir, in lines 17 and 18 you said that there were parallel municipal authorities made up of Albanians exclusively. Let me just remind you that these answers related to some reports being filed and this is the answer that you gave in which you stated that there existed parallel municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I'm not clear about this. What kind of parallel structures are you talking about? At school things were segregated. The Albanian teachers were teaching separately, but they were not being paid by the Serbian state like their fellow Serb fellow teachers. Albanian teachers were paid for by the Albanian villages, if you're talking about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to try and read this in my poor English. [In English] " ... you had no one to complain to, because we had -- we had a parallel municipal authority in which the Albanians were predominant ..." [Interpretation] Then you go on: [In English] " ... but we had -- we had no reason to go to these police stations."

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: As for complaining, that's true that we had nowhere to complain to because nobody was dealing with our complaints, but there was a human rights organisation which had oriented the population, the Albanian population, whenever they had any complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the previous sentence, the one that speaks about the parallel municipal authority dominated by the Albanians or made up exclusively by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It's exactly what I said earlier. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you to give us an explanation of what you said earlier. Can you please do that.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Again, I'm not clear, but parallel structure, separate offices in the municipality there weren't. There were kind of offices in private homes. There were offices for the LDK or the human rights organisation. These were the offices. Otherwise, I don't know what to say. This is what I've thought about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So this is what you meant by parallel municipal offices; is that right? Mr. Latifi, where did you go to the secondary school, and which school did you finish?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The first two years I studied in the village, whereas the third and the fourth in Prizren, in the gymnasium there. That's where I finished the secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that at the time, high schools were made up of mixed ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The middle schools were mixed. All communities went there. There was Serbs there, there were Turks, and Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
