utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me when did you drop out of the university where you studied agriculture in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I left in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that the Faculty of Agriculture in Pristina continue its work after 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, not in a regular sort of way. In 1991, I attended school in the facilities of the university, but the rest after that was in private homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did the Faculty of Agriculture as part of the University of Pristina continue to work and to function?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: For us Albanians, it didn't continue; for the Serbs, yes. Because we were moved out of the university facilities. So teaching was organised in private people's homes. The hostels were closed down to us. We had no right to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the faculty. Who removed you from the Faculty of Agriculture in Pristina? I'm talking about your university studies. Who suspended you from the university?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It was the regime then. They would ask us students to accept the curricula drafted by the Serb regime; and since we did not agree with those, we were forced to leave. That's what the rector's office told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Latifi. You say that you continued to be involved in farming. From the time when you dropped out of university and when you returned from Pristina, did you continue this job in Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Since I left the faculty, I continued to be involved in agriculture in my home village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say in your statement that in the spring of 1998 three bodies were found and that those were civilians who had nothing to do with the KLA. First let me ask you this, Mr. Latifi: What is the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: A military organisation organised by the people themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what you know about who the organisers were and how this organisation was set up?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Up until then, no, but I learnt about it after the war; but up until, then I knew nothing about the organisation. If you want me to tell you what I learnt after the war ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Mr. Latifi. All I'm asking you about pertains to the period of 1998 and 1999 or some previous period; however, I'm not interested in what you learned afterwards. All I'm asking you about relates to this specific period that I mentioned. Why did you then say that these three killed civilians were not members of the KLA if you didn't know anything about them?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: These three villagers, they were working in the field. They were irrigating a maize field, and they had worked there all day. And how can someone who works the fields belong to a military organisation? They've all their lives been involved in agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say, Mr. Latifi, that actually you don't know how these three persons died, and you never witnessed their deaths?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: That's correct, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me go back to the KLA now. In the summer of 1998, was there any fighting in Orahovac, Retimlje, Dubrava, Zociste, in this area where you were living? I'm talking about the period between the 17th of July to 25th or 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: During that time, there was fighting in those villages, not in the particular place where I was living, in Rahovec, yes, because we heard explosions, we've seen smoke billowing, because we could see from a distance - we're about 7 kilometres away - but you could see the smoke billowing. And we've also seen refugees who left those villages coming towards us. They told us about what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what you heard, what was going on in Orahovac in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: According to the eye-witnesses, we heard that there were killings, there were houses burnt down, and people being forced out of their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the fighting broke out, who was in control of Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It was the Serb police, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, then who attacked the Serb police and that attack resulted in fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, you also say that in September of 1998 the police and the army withdrew from the area where you lived. Where did you get this information from, and what did you specifically had in mind when you say that they withdrew?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Where they were initially deployed, they were not there. They were seen on the main road clearly. They would move along the Piran-Prizren frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... uniformed personnel who were controlling the Prizren-Djakovica road?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: They were deployed in the vineyards of Landovica, the regular army, whereas at the entrance of Dushanov there was a check-point, a 24-hour check-point. That check-point was removed, and I knew that they set it up infrequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 24th, or rather, do you know when the bombing started in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The bombing started in the evening on the 24th of March. We saw the first aircraft which flew in the Kosovo skies and that was at 20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear any explosions in the vicinity of Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: From the NATO aircraft you mean? No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what did you do on the 25th of March, 1999, on the morning of the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: On the 25th of March, the village was encircled. There was some shelling, small-scale shelling initially, then they stopped, then the regular army with tanks and armoured vehicles moved in. Then we started to withdraw from the village, and we noted that some houses started burning and by 11.00 the village was emptied out. Some went -- most of the people went to Mamusha village, whereas some 800 of us went toward Serbica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, would you please focus on my questions. My question was: What did you do on the morning of the 25th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: We stayed in the house of a cousin, and we were observing from where the forces were coming, and we tried to find out what was happening because the forces had most of the time gone through without damaging anything but we noticed on that particular day that things were changing, houses were being damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, you just told us that you were not in your house. In whose house were you on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: On the 24th of March, I was in my own house because the -- my house is next to the main road; and then the next day, we went to my cousin's house, which was away from the main road where the big movement was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the name of that cousin of yours?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Xhevat Dalipi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you move to Xhevat Dalipi's house on the 25th?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: On the 24th of March in the evening we went because the same day we had a victim, we had to bury a cousin of ours, but in the evening we got together in that house. They had a big cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you all get together because of the bombing that had started, or because actually it was announced that the war was going to start on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: We're not afraid of the bombing because they hadn't -- they weren't coming to bomb us, but we knew that something was going to happen the following day, that's why we joined each other. It was a very good idea that we came together, judging from what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, where was Xhevat Dalipi's house in the village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It was somewhere in the east of the village. It's further away from the main road, about 800 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it fair to say that this house was also in a plain?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No. There were many more houses around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose there were lots of houses surrounding your house as well?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: There were not many houses because the entrance to my house is -- my house is clearly on the plain. There are no other houses except for two of my uncle's -- three, actually. Then there is the road, there are some houses on the other side, but they were sparsely built houses in that area. There weren't many houses. But my uncle's house was surrounded by many houses. The houses are more concentrated there, in that part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, where did you spend the night between the 24th and the 25th, in which particular part of the house?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: In one of the rooms of my uncle's house. That's where all of us stayed, because there are four rooms in the cellar but we stayed in one room, all of us. So we stayed there all of us. There was no chance to sleep that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe it may be time for another technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will have the break now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, in your statement you mentioned that the villagers of Pirane divided into two groups, that one of these groups went to the village of Mamusa, approximately 80 per cent of the population, 1.900 people more or less, and that the remaining population went to Srbica. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct but it's not Skenderaj in Albanian, it's Serbica, the village. It is correct that 1.900, approximately, went to -- towards Mamusha, whereas 800 towards Serbica village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Always have this problem when you say Donja Srbica, it is only Donja Srbica, whereas Skenderaj is another municipality. This is the village of Donja Srbica, am I right, and there is no alternative name for this village? I believe you clarified that earlier in the Milutinovic transcript. What time was it when you left Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I believe it was about 8.00 a.m., between 8.00 and 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I forgot something. That morning you said you couldn't sleep all night long. Can you tell me at 4.00 a.m. was it already day? Was it daylight?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: At 4.00 a.m. the day had already begun to break, but it is complete daylight at 8.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction at 5.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the visibility like or what was is like at 4.00 a.m. on the 25th of March of any given year?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: You can scarcely see, but you can hear very well because it's very quiet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, I would like to know how you came up with the conclusion that on March the 15th [as interpreted] at 4.00 a.m. your village was surrounded by Serbian police and military units with tanks and different other vehicles and a large number of men?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Because we could hear the noise, the rattle of the tanks, they stopped initially at the Pirane bridge and that near the cooperative building, near the school, there was a parking-lot there. So we could hear the noise as to where they were coming from and where they were stopping. And once it dawned, we could see very well that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far was this school from the house in which you were at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: About 500 metres far I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the parking-lot, how far was that one?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Approximately the same distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And from these places the village started to be shelled; is that correct? Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The shelling we believed was coming from Landovica village, from that direction, and from the bridge, the village bridge. You can see the bridge very clearly. It is somewhere in the centre of the village, whereas the police was or the army were about 400 metres away from the place where the shells fell. The shelling was brief. Then at around 7.30 in the morning the infantry forces began to climb in the direction of Ratishe village. They stationed themselves above the village which was about 100 metres away from the house where we were at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, what is the distance between Landovica and Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: As the crow flies, about 4 kilometres I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the military forces and the police forces encircled your village that morning. How could you then leave that village to go in the direction of Mamusa and the Donja Srbica?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Part of the population that left towards Mamusha left earlier. There was an open corridor, so to say the army was there first so they would not stop the population. Then this corridor was closed down. The other remaining corridor was through the village towards Serbica village, and we passed through that corridor. The police was about 20 or 30 metres away and another group a little bit lower, but they did not stop us, they allowed us to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this means that the village was not encircled, it was not entirely encircled when it was shelled?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: There were forces at the entry to the village at the school, at the cooperative facility, then there was presence at the road leading to Randubrave village and Krusha e Vogel village. And at the graveyard of Mamusha village there was also presence of forces. These are the entry points to the village. There's no other entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see Mamusa from the house in which you were?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, no, you couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You can't see it, but according to your story it would appear that the Serbian forces shelled themselves. They came into the village, stopped, and then the shells started to fall on them and on your house as well.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No. What I said is different. While they were stationed at the school, at the cooperative, and at the bridge, they began to shell the centre of the village. They were about 400 metres away from the place where the first shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And these shells that came in the direction of Landovica, where did they fall?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The first shells hit the mosque. They fell somewhere between the minaret and the building of the mosque itself. You could see it very well. The second shell fell in the courtyard of the mosque, and the distance between the mosque and the location where the police was stationed was about 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And where is the school located within the village?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Near the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The cooperative facility is also near the main road. The distance between the schools and the cooperative building is approximately 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there was an evacuation group which you organised earlier. Who organised it and how it all came about that you organised this evacuation group?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Some youths from the village, learning from what had happened in earlier offensives, organised this plan for evacuation, to direct the population towards the corridors that were open and through which you could leave the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These young people were not members of the KLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. They were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It means that whoever was a civilian in your mind could not be a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think they were members of the KLA. Not until that time at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did I understand you well earlier today, during your testimony you said that you heard about the KLA for the first time after the war?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I did hear that there were KLA forces. I didn't know where they were operating, but I learned about this organisation in detail later on, after the war, and I also read books about the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, please tell me whether in your village there is a facility of the company called Kosovo Vino?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: This is in Krusha e Vogel village, which means it's nearby, it's about 3 kilometres far from our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Latifi. Did you hear that on the 1st of February, 1999, the security of the company Kosovo Vino in Mala Krusa was disarmed by members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about this; however, the same question was put to me in one of the previous trials. But again, I'm telling you that I did not hear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Please tell me whether you knew the family called Xhafiqi from Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Are you referring to Ymer Xhafiqi?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ymer Xhafiqi, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Ymer Xhafiqi was kidnapped in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I heard a day later that Ymer Xhafiqi was kidnapped, but I don't know who kidnapped him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please correct me if I'm wrong. Did Ymer Xhafiqi work at Prizren?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And he was an inspector of the Prizren SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: He worked where the identity cards and passports were issued, in that office where the travel documents were issued. That's where he worked. I don't know what his post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And his father, I believe, worked as a forestry man until he retired; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: He was a vineyard guard until he retired. He worked for Progres company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is their house situated in Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: They used to have one, but they sold it. It was in the middle, approximately in the middle of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was it close to the house in which you were on the 25th of March, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It wasn't far from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Latifi, on page 4 of your statement; in the Albanian this is paragraph 3 in English this is page 4, paragraph 2. You stated that members of the KLA usually filmed or took pictures of bodies and graves. Did you find that paragraph? It is the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are talking about the events in 1999 during the course of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How did you know that these people were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: There were two people then and they were in uniform and they were carrying weapons -- carrying light automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which village they came from?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Which village they came from?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from. I saw them there, but I didn't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you see those people after the war?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, I never saw them afterwards. Obviously they were not from our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there Albanians also living at Donja Srbica?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, there were Albanians and Serb as well as Romes or Ashkali as they are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you yourself did not leave with the group that moved in a convoy. You yourself stayed at Donja Srbica for approximately additional ten days; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, with my family together with the 86 members of my family we stayed there for another ten days because there was no place in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that you are not an eye-witness of the killing of a man called Rexhep who you -- whose body you found later on -- whose body you found at Randobrava?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, I only saw him killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that you were not an eye-witness of the death of 25 people buried in Donji Retimlje?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: When they were killed, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it fair to say that you don't know who shot Xhafer Elshani?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: The Serbs who were stationed above Serbica, they carried regular army uniforms, and we knew about this from the Serbs who lived in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that no documents were seized from you?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Where are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean when you reached the border, no documents were seized from you; right?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: All that we had, with the exception of the driving licence which I had hidden, concealed in the Pampers of my second son.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Nappies, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, how far is Donja Srbica from Pirane?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: It's about 3 kilometres, 2 and a half, in aerial distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what about Donji Retimlje?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: About 5 kilometres, I think. I'm not accurate about this. I'm not sure about the accuracy of this figure, but it's approximate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I'm asking you about approximate distances. I'm sure you can't give me the accurate ones. On the last page you say that members of the KLA had buried the family in the vicinity of Randobrava. Can you see that? It's page 3, paragraph 8; and in English it's page 3, also paragraph 8. Mr. Latifi, did you understand my question, or do I need to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In this passage that you have just read to yourself, you mention again members of the KLA by saying that they had buried these bodies. This incident also happened during the war. Am I right, Mr. Latifi?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, during the war, after the 25th of March. It happened sometime on the 26th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ask these men, Who are you? What are you doing? Where did you come from?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that in your area there were members of the KLA at the time when you were there as well?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: In my village and in Randubrave and Serbica there were no KLA fighters stationed. They may have been on the move time and again, but they usually conducted movements during the night; and we didn't have a chance to see them or maybe they did it for security reasons. I cannot deny that there were, but stationed regularly -- regular deployment, as such, I didn't notice during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that the Serbian forces were engaged in fighting with these forces in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAHIM LATIFI
utterances.text: I don't know what to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Latifi. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Is there any re-examination, Ms. Nilsen?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, there will be no further questions from the Prosecution. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Latifi, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber has your statement and your transcript of evidence from before and the answers you've been able to give today. We're grateful that you've been able to come again to The Hague to assist, and you may now, of course, go back to your normal activities and the court officer will assist you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That appears to be a convenient time, Ms. Nilsen, or perhaps Ms. Kravetz I see sitting there. Little point in using six minutes with a new witness. We will adjourn then until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 13th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.40 p.m.,
